featured.name: Polaris
featured.fact: The North Star, and a Cepheid variable: it pulses gently in brightness about every four days.

featured.name: Mizar
featured.fact: Look for faint Alcor right beside it: telling the two apart was a traditional test of eyesight.

featured.name: Dubhe
featured.fact: One of the Pointers: extend the line from Merak through Dubhe about five times its length to reach Polaris.

featured.name: Thuban
featured.fact: It was the pole star about 4,500 years ago, when the Egyptians built the pyramids at Giza.

source: Yale Bright Star Catalogue, 5th revised ed. (Hoffleit & Warren 1991), CDS catalogue V/50; facts: see docs/night-sky-facts.md
